description: The design-source render oracle wiring (exit criterion E7, guardrail G-11). Per frame the oracle imports the committed Figma fixture (corpus/figma-fixtures/<name>.json), compiles it through dashc's compile_figma (Profile::Core), loads and re-solves it with the TaffySolver — running the typesetter measure seam so TEXT nodes size to their shaped extent — renders the committed scene with the Skia reference painter (text painted from a GlyphRunTable staged over the committed Noto atlases, story #303), and diffs that fresh render against the committed Figma design-source PNG (Figma's REST GET /images export) within the frame's per-rule tolerance band. The reference is OUR render of the imported fixture, not a pre-committed corpus golden — so the diff measures the reference painter against Figma's own render of the same scene at the same size. The harness and the bands live in goldens/tooling/src/oracle.rs; the diff runs in goldens/tooling/tests/render_oracle.rs (the_reference_renders_match_their_design_source), un-gated because it is hermetic (committed fixture + committed design source + in-process compile_figma, no network) and fast. A frame is captured by setting its figmaNodeId and running `deno task oracle-capture` (the Figma file key is joined from the fixture's entry in corpus/figma-fixtures/manifest.json rather than repeated here, debt #338) (importers/figma); that step downloads Figma's GET /images render into design-source/<frame>.png and flips the frame's designSource and status to captured.

gate.reason: The oracle measures all 7 frames, each within its band. Two layout frames on aa-edge: v08-wrap (0.000%) and v08-grid-spans (0.037%, tightened from 0.116% when story #385 committed Inter and matched the family by name). Two shadow frames on blur-falloff: v08-drop-shadow (0.022%) and v08-inner-shadow (0.000%). Three text frames on msdf-text: v05-text-latin (0.033%), v06-text-arabic (1.405%), and v08-baseline (1.816%). Every fixture is self-authored in the project's own account (G-11) in the committed corpus fonts, and the text frames render through the text render path (#303), so each text frame measures the reference painter against Figma's render of the same font, not a substitution. Two frames caught real bugs the self-oracle goldens missed: v06-text-arabic a line-height bug — the typesetter took a line's height from the cascade's primary font — fixed in #314 (3.300% to 1.405%); and v08-baseline the box-bottom baseline drift — a text leaf aligned on its box bottom, not its glyph baseline, because Taffy's high-level measure reports no leaf baseline — fixed for #272 by a post-solve glyph-baseline correction in dashscene-engine (3.807% to 1.816%). The gate names issue #265 (the manual-fixture tracking issue); no design source is fabricated (the self-oracle failure G-11 forbids), and every frame is captured. E7 (the design-source render oracle) is MET. The v0.9 exit gate (#49) asserts E1 through E7.

frames.note: Layout frame (E3 wrap; story #46). The committed fixture imports and renders to 420x184 and diffs within the aa-edge band against Figma's GET /images render of node 1:10. Hard rect edges — the aa-edge band.

Layout frame (E3 grid spans; story #46). The committed fixture imports and renders to 720x480 and diffs within the aa-edge band against Figma's GET /images render of node 1:11. The five structural cells (span/fill/minmax/fixed placement and positions) match the export pixel-exact. The sixth cell is a 'hug me' TEXT leaf: with the text render path wired (story #303) its HUG box sizes to the shaped text (no longer collapsing to its padding box), so the grid solves as Figma laid it out and no region is excluded. The whole 720x480 frame diffs 127 px (0.037%) — the residual is MSDF glyph edges, well within the 2% aa-edge budget. It measured 401 px (0.116%) until story #385, whose Inter corpus and family-name matching removed the Latin glyph-shape substitution that made up most of it: the 'hug me' cell is authored in Inter, and until the cascade carried Inter and matched a family by name the oracle rendered it in Noto Sans. Story #385 landed this cascade change here because the E7 freeze lifted when #49 closed; docs/decisions/corpus-ships-inter.md had deferred exactly this consequence to whoever closed it. This is now the only committed frame that measures Inter against Figma's own render. Hard rect edges — the aa-edge band.

Mixed-size baseline row (E3 baseline case, story #46; fixture authored by the fixture-author text-baseline command). Three Noto Sans Regular runs — 'small' (12), 'medium' (24), 'LARGE' (40) — baseline-aligned in a fixed 380x120 frame, all in the committed corpus/atlas/ascii font, so the oracle measures the reference painter against Figma's render of the SAME font. This frame replaces the earlier Inter-authored lowering-baseline fixture, whose Latin leaves the committed corpus did not provide (rendered in Noto Sans its HUG root measured 621x160 against Figma's 608x160 and could not be diffed). It caught a real engine bug the self-oracle goldens missed: the diff first measured 3.807% against the msdf-text band's 3% budget because Taffy's high-level measure reports no baseline for a leaf, so a text leaf aligned on its box bottom, not its glyph baseline (#272), and the shorter runs sat a descender too low. Fixed by a post-solve glyph-baseline correction in dashscene-engine, which brought it to 828/45600 px (1.816%). Measured in the msdf-text band, not aa-edge: once the layout is correct the residual is glyph edges plus the small reference-vs-Figma first-line ascent-metric difference, the same nature as v05-text-latin and v06-text-arabic. The baseline-alignment geometry itself is proven exactly by the engine unit test a_mixed_size_text_baseline_row_aligns_on_glyph_baselines, not by this pixel diff. The msdf-text band.

Soft drop shadow (story #45; fixture authored by the fixture-author drop-shadow command, #304). One 40x40 rounded card with a DROP_SHADOW (offset y=4, blur 6, spread 0, black alpha 0.55) centered in a 96x96 light frame, lowering clean under Profile::Core. The committed fixture imports and renders to 96x96 and diffs 2/9216 px (0.022%) against Figma's GET /images render of node 1:2 — within the blur-falloff band. This is the first real measurement of the sigma = blur/2 mapping (G-1, docs/decisions/effects-vocabulary-shadows.md) against Figma: near-pixel-exact confirms it. The blur-falloff band. The blur-falloff band gained a gate at the #422 ruling (threshold 40, budget 1 %) beside its 12 % residual, and this frame is one of the two the band governs. Measured: healthy 0.022 % on the residual and 0.000 % at the gate; with the drop shadow removed, 4.351 % and 2.930 %. The removal passes the residual at a third of its budget and fails the gate at 2.9x — that is what this frame would have to contain to fail, measured, and before the gate it would have stayed green with the effect gone.

Soft inner shadow (story #45; fixture authored by the fixture-author inner-shadow command, #304). One 40x40 rounded card with an INNER_SHADOW (offset 0, blur 6, spread 0, black alpha 0.55) centered in a 96x96 light frame, lowering clean under Profile::Core. The committed fixture imports and renders to 96x96 and diffs 0/9216 px (0.000%) against Figma's GET /images render of node 1:2 — pixel-exact, within the blur-falloff band. Same sigma = blur/2 pinning as the drop shadow. The blur-falloff band. The blur-falloff band gained a gate at the #422 ruling (threshold 40, budget 1 %) beside its 12 % residual, and this frame is one of the two the band governs. Measured: healthy 0.000 % on the residual and 0.000 % at the gate; with the inner shadow removed, 3.570 % and 2.018 %. The removal passes the residual and fails the gate at 2.0x — the tightest reproducible margin against the gate, so this frame is the one that binds the number. What it does not pin is the sigma mapping: doubling the shadow sigma measures 4.536 % on the residual and only 0.206 % at the gate, so both terms pass it (issue #412).

Arabic RTL text as MSDF atlas quads (E2; fixture authored by the fixture-author text-arabic command, #304). A banner, a harakat word, and an Arabic-Indic numeral readout, all Noto Sans Arabic Regular (the committed corpus/atlas/arabic font). The committed fixture imports and renders to 520x240 and diffs 1753/124800 px (1.405%) against Figma's GET /images render of node 1:2 — within the msdf-text band. This frame CAUGHT a real bug the self-oracle goldens missed: before story #314 the diff was 3.300% (just over the band) because the typesetter took a line's height from the cascade's primary (Latin) font, so the stacked Arabic lines were measured too short and drifted; #314 derives line height per line from the fonts that shaped it, bringing this to 1.405%. The residual is fine glyph-edge and line-metric difference vs Figma's raster, well within budget. The msdf-text band.

Latin text as MSDF atlas quads (fixture authored by the fixture-author text-latin command, #304). 'Hello dashscene' (28) and '88 mph' (44), both Noto Sans Regular — the committed corpus/atlas/ascii font, so the oracle measures the reference painter against Figma's render of the SAME font, not a substitution. The committed fixture imports and renders to 480x200 and diffs 32/96000 px (0.033%) against Figma's GET /images render of node 1:2 — near-pixel-exact, deep inside the msdf-text band. Confirms the msdf-text band and the text render path (#303). The msdf-text band.
